Arm A: a router-caused failure at the http tier walked http, browser and claude and returned 'app: all fetch tiers exhausted for … (attempted: http, browser, claude)' — 3 engine invocations per failure. Arm B: 1 invocation and the error reaches the caller as itself ('config: missing [claude] api key'), which also gives the operator's row its origin for free with no worker.rs change. The un-skip at fetcher.rs:752 is the same fix and the same line: arm A logged 'http tier un-skipped: browser engine failed' on a config error and spent the tier the router had correctly skipped; arm B leaves the skip standing (http invoked 0 times) while an Error::Browser still un-skips it — the paired assertion. One carrier: the predicate on the existing typed enum, no header, no sentinel message, no second flag; the source's defect is two mechanisms (in-band marker plus a RouterError that escapes the loop and renders as a 400). Orthogonality preserved: is_terminal_for_job untouched, and the predicate is an exhaustive match with no wildcard, so the default is theirs and a new variant stops the build until someone decides. falsifier: The proposal's own falsifier fires and the direction understated it: a static census, not a jobs-table query (no retained DB in the worktree), finds NO producer of an ours-error on the ladder path today. Error::Config is minted only by Config::load/validate and Catalog::load (boot-time; validate() closes 29 cases before the server starts) and by no engine crate; Error::Transact comes from Browser::transact, which the ladder never calls; Error::ReplayMiss is raised at the AppContext chokepoint above the ladder; plugin errors never reach a fetch tier. So the amplification is real and now closed, but currently unreachable in production — the break arm is a guard, not a repair. Return condition: the first engine that types a misconfiguration as Error::Config at call time (the remote fabric and the archive engine are the likely first), or the first failed job row carrying 'config:' or 'plugin:' from a fetch tier. Also unfixed by design: the measurable the study stated as 'tiers × max_attempts → 1' cannot be reached by this context, which is forbidden from touching is_terminal_for_job — the max_attempts factor lives on that axis and Error::Config stays retryable at the job level. What moved is tiers → 1 per attempt.

technique: lease-renewal (absent is not lost; teardown is a held state)
subject: job-coordination

return_condition: When the lease moves to a store separate from the jobs table (shared Redis, a second instance); meanwhile: read the heartbeat result at worker.rs:861 and stop the task on false.

RETURNING); crates/core/src/app.rs:955 ScrapeApp::target_key default None; crates/core/migrations/0041_job_target_key.sql; crates/server/src/mcp/mod.rs:650 target_key_for (the one door helper, sibling of validate_app_params) called from all six enqueue doors; fixture crates/server/src/e2e/target_exclusion.rs

The paired assertions are what keep the fix from being the per-app cap in disguise and both PASS in arm A too: two jobs of the same app with DIFFERENT target keys still peak at 2, and two jobs with a NULL key peak at 2 (an app that has not overridden target_key is not serialised against every other). subject: convergence-loop-and-requeue
seam: crates/core/src/storage.rs:150 requeue_after(error, attempts, stated) -> Requeue (pure, now-free) + :100 ladder_delay + :55 FailReason (Typed|Text) + :690 Storage::fail; crates/engine-http/src/lib.rs:950 budget_exhausted carries the stated wait it could not honour; crates/core/src/error.rs Error::http_after/stated_retry_after; crates/core/migrations/0042_job_requeue_reason.sql; fixture crates/server/src/e2e/requeue_policy.rs
seam_notes: Measured A/B in-tree by disabling the policy's two opinionated arms and re-running the fixture on the trait-level fake seam (a scripted HttpClient an app reaches through ctx.engines.http and propagates with ?, which is how every API-shaped app in crates/apps raises a transport failure). Arm A: an origin stating Retry-After 600 cost 3 engine invocations inside a one-minute observation window (the ladder placed retries at 10s and 20s, both inside it) and a config error burned 3 attempts. Arm B: 1 invocation with available_at at least 600s out, and 1 attempt. The harness fast-forwards only delays that fall INSIDE the window - a wait we are not allowed to shorten ends the loop instead of being simulated through, which is the whole point of the stated-wait arm. The control (an ordinary connection reset) rides all three attempts in both arms. Third number: a table test over one instance of every variant the policy has no opinion about asserts the default arm is byte-identical to 10*2^attempts capped at 3600; jitter stays a property of the write (job id + attempt seed), not of the policy, and only ever lengthens, so a stated wait is never shortened by the spread. The registry's rule that giving up must be visible is honoured by jobs.requeue_reason ('attempt ladder' | 'server-stated wait' | 'store contention' | 'ours-class failure'), without which this trades a predictable ladder for a smarter opaque one. One carrier: the retry_after field on Error::Http, minted at the single site that learns and abandons a stated wait, never a sentinel in the message. Gate on branch direction/kube-rs-round5: cargo test --workspace green (6 new unit + 3 new e2e), cargo clippy --workspace --tests clean, cargo fmt --check clean.
falsifier: The carrier does NOT survive the tiered fetcher: fetcher.rs's ladder_exhausted flattens every tier failure into Error::App('all fetch tiers exhausted ...'), so a stated wait learned on the http tier is lost for apps that fetch through ctx.fetch, and the arm only fires for the eleven raw-HTTP apps that call ctx.engines.http directly (which are the API-shaped ones that actually meet 429s). Stated in the fixture and in the fetch-chokepoint inventory row rather than papered over. Also not taken: the direction's pre-acceptance base rate (share of failed rows carrying a 429/503-with-wait or a config:/plugin: prefix) - no retained history in the worktree.

subject: error-handling
seam: crates/core/src/error.rs:155 CauseValue (boxed cause + the type name captured at the raise site) + Error::{http,browser,parse,config}_from constructors + Error::cause()/cause_kind()/cause_chain(); crates/engine-http/src/lib.rs:887 transport_error (the one reqwest mapping, retryable arm keeps the reqwest::Error); crates/core/migrations/0043_job_cause_kind.sql; guard crates/core/tests/error_cause_chain.rs

The guard was run against a deliberately reverted site to prove it fires (4 found, 3 allowed). Paired assertion: 22 sites DO attach a cause, so the guard cannot pass by nobody raising these variants any more. Display is untouched and every message still interpolates its cause, so no job row's text moved - what is added is the value beside the sentence. Consumer proofs: a real refused connection (127.0.0.1:1) classifies through the cause with is_connect()/is_timeout()/is_decode() and NO string in the assertion; a failed job row records cause_kind = 'toml::de::error::Error' while a text-only failure records NULL; GET /jobs/{id}/receipt renders cause_kind and requeue_reason beside the sentence. The boundary is stated in the module docs: is_terminal_for_job and is_router_failure still match on the variant, exhaustively, and must never consult a source. Gate on branch direction/kube-rs-round5: cargo test --workspace green (4 new guard/round-trip cases + 1 engine-http case), cargo clippy --workspace --tests clean, cargo fmt --check clean.
falsifier: Two honest deviations. (1) The direction's headline '186 sites' is a workspace-wide count across all fourteen String variants; re-measured for the four variants with the guard's own rule it is 18 in the two governed crates (30 across all of crates/), and crates/apps constructs none of the four at all. The remaining ~11 sites outside the governed crates are deliberately NOT pinned - the pattern spreads into them, and pinning the workspace would turn a landing into a rewrite. (2) The chain is exposed as Error::cause()/cause_chain() rather than through std::error::Error::source, because thiserror's #[source] cannot take an Option<Box<dyn Error>> and a non-optional wrapper would make every causeless failure report a source that renders as nothing. A generic error-chain walker therefore still sees nothing under these variants. Return condition: thiserror gaining optional source fields, at which point the derive replaces the accessor.

Under both arms every case ends the same way, because the counted list (fuel, linear memory, tables, instances) is already published in GET /plugins telemetry (fuel_budget, memory_bytes_cap; lib.rs:102-112) and the uncounted list is empty by construction: the plugins import nothing, so there is no host call in which wall time or host-side allocation could escape the count. subject: self-healing
seam: crates/server/src/worker.rs:815-831 (catch_unwind around app.run(ctx), with the source comment that enumerates what it CANNOT catch: a non-yielding wedge, and a hard abort via process::exit/OOM/SIGKILL - for both the reaper is the backstop and can only report "lease expired (heartbeat stale)") and crates/server/src/worker.rs:790-812 (AppContext, which carries spent_usd: Arc<SpentTotal>, the progress reporter, the checkpointer and the research cache across the would-be process boundary)
arms: A = today, work item as an in-process async task with unwind caught. B = the technique, one child process per work item, parent classifies from the child. Three real failure classes from the tree own comment: (1) panic -> equivalent, B buys nothing and costs a spawn; (2) non-yielding wedge -> B better, a true verdict instead of a stale-lease label; (3) hard abort -> B clearly better, only the child dies and sibling jobs on the same worker survive.
why_not_better: Two of three cases favour B and it still loses. The work item decrements a live shared spend counter (Arc<SpentTotal>, an AtomicU64) as it spends; that does not serialize into an invocation. Across a process boundary a child that spends and then hard-aborts in case 3 has consumed budget the parent never observed - reopening the record-precedes-effect window the fork was bought to close. In one address space the counter is updated before the spend call returns and the law holds for free.
structural_fact: The tree ALREADY forks one layer in: crates/engine-claude/src/lib.rs:155-159 spawns the model CLI as a child process. What crosses that boundary is a request and a response; what would cross the outer one is an accounting reference. Nobody wrote a policy saying "fork where the state is small" - the boundary landed where the mutable state stopped. This tree applies the technique and declines it, correctly, in one call stack.
return_condition: When the cost ledger becomes write-ahead - a store the work item appends to BEFORE spending. The shape is already half present: spend is restored from checkpoints and cost events are recorded. Once it exists the disqualifier dissolves and case 3 wins outright; re-run this A/B then.

seam: crates/server/src/mcp/mod.rs:490 clamp_budget (private to the MCP module, called only from the four tool handlers at :502,:522,:534) vs crates/server/src/routes/jobs.rs:47 validate_budget_usd. enqueue_app takes the ceiling as an ARGUMENT, so the rail is the door's property, not the engine's. docs/features/mcp.md asserted "an agent cannot ask its way past the operator's rail".
measurable: doors onto one engine whose spend rail diverges, and how many tests see it. Arm A (before): 2 diverge, 0 of 5 mcp tests observe it. Arm B (after): 2 diverge, 1 of 6 observes it.
what_a_caught_outcome_would_teach: that the rail sits at the engine's admission path rather than at the surface - which would have been a stronger rule than the amendment states, and would have become its second half. The seam could return a result that changed the landing, so it was a falsifier and not a confirmation.
result: NOT caught. The doors diverge on identical input: clamp_budget(Some(100.0),1.0)=1.0 against validate_budget_usd(Some(100.0))=Ok(Some(100.0)); and the sharpest row, an OMITTED budget_usd, gives the MCP caller the operator's rail and the REST caller NO ceiling at all. Both doors are mounted on the same unauthenticated localhost listener.
structural_fact: the tree documents the asymmetry in its own refusal text (routes/jobs.rs:53 tells a rejected caller to "enqueue over MCP, where the [mcp] max_job_budget_usd rail treats 0 as a real $0 ceiling") - so the authors knew the doors differ, while the feature doc's summary sentence read as a claim about the deployment. Nobody designed that gap; it fell out of putting the clamp in the surface module.
change: one paired characterization test pinning the divergence (mcp::tests::the_budget_rail_is_this_doors_property_not_the_engines), `mod jobs` widened to pub(crate) so the test can reach the other door, and the doc sentence qualified with *on this door* plus a paragraph naming what the two switches actually bound. The REST door was deliberately NOT clamped: the operator is inside the trust boundary, which is the technique's own reasoning.
gate: cargo test -p pumper-server --bin pumper - 507 passed, 0 failed, 4 ignored (was 506 before the added test).
falsifier: the test was SHOWN to fail: perturbing validate_budget_usd to clamp at 1.0 turned it red (left Ok(Some(1.0)), right Ok(Some(100.0))), and the perturbation was reverted. A characterization test never shown to fail is indistinguishable from one that cannot.
return_condition: when the two doors converge - if a future change moves the rail into enqueue_app or the admission path, the test goes red, and the right response is to delete it and correct the doc rather than to restore the divergence

subject: machine-paced-delivery
seam: scripts/docs/check-doc-sync.mjs:285 (`if (payload.stop_hook_active) process.exit(0)`) + the three-state exit contract at :248-266, wired via .claude/settings.json hooks.Stop
seam_note: This gate corrected the technique twice. It mutates nothing and BLOCKS nothing (its own header: 'Nothing here ever blocks') -- and it still guards re-entry, because exit 2 feeds a reminder to the model, the model acts, acting ends another turn, and the turn end re-fires the hook. So the termination contract is created by the gate's output RE-ENTERING THE AGENT'S LOOP, not by blocking and not by mutation; advisory is the weakest tier and the one most likely to ship unguarded. Technique redrafted twice mid-run to the three-tier form (advisory / blocking / mutating). Second corroboration: the hook's recorded history is the liveness paragraph made concrete -- it detected nothing for its entire life, replayed over all 31 transcripts, 1,136 Edit/Write calls, ZERO detections, because its turn-boundary scan stopped at the first user-role entry and 3,837 of 4,187 user-role entries are tool results. Ran green every turn and was indistinguishable from a working gate. Reached gate-liveness's three-state contract (0 pass / 2 model-actionable / 3 could-not-run) independently, after being burned by exactly that failure.
ship_reason: the gate already implements the technique's re-entry rule; nothing to change -- this is a confirming tree, read-only
return_condition: counters on the re-entry path and the could-not-run path, both currently unobservable: a gate that has never reported a skip and a gate whose skip path is broken look identical

seam_note: Amendment landed this run: a bounding stage's failure path is correlated with the input it was bounding, so the involuntary fallback emits its largest payload where the transform was most needed - and it is invisible to the elected-recovery rate. Walked against three real sites in this tree and the amendment did NOT hold at two of them, which is the honest result. [remote] max_body_bytes and PARTIAL_CAP_CHARS (4000) both cap their fallbacks below the trigger, as the amendment prescribes. The third, MAX_SHIM_COMMAND_LINE at :800, states the amendment's disclosure rule in the tree's own words - ':838, a refusal is loud, a truncated command line is not' - and REFUSES rather than truncating, which is stronger than what the amendment asks for. Residue is one site: envelope_text's raw-result fallback is bounded only by what the CLI returned and carries no marker saying the payload is raw rather than structured.
